source: CARDI (2011), "Handbook of Integrated Techniques for Increasing Wet-Season and Dry-Season Rice Productivity" (Khmer, 50pp, funded by CAVAC/ACIAR, foreword by H.E. Chan Sarun, Minister of Agriculture, dated 26 August 2011)
text: Two other pest/disease problems are briefly noted in the same integrated pest management section. Stem borer larvae ('dangkov roung', boring into the stem) kill the growing point from tillering onward, causing 'deadheart' (dying central shoot) up through heading, when the same damage causes 'whitehead' (a sterile, whitened panicle); damage is present everywhere but rarely reaches an economically damaging level except at the tillering stage, when it can replace enough tillers to reduce yield — heavy infestation is most common in densely-planted fields with high humidity and temperature favoring larval survival, so avoiding excessive planting density is again the key preventive step; if heavy moth activity is observed at tillering or booting, flooding the field to fully submerge the crop for about a week can suppress egg-laying. Using varieties with a similar, synchronized flowering time within one area (or timing planting so flowering coincides with neighboring fields) is described as the most effective non-chemical control, since scattered flowering times give the moth a continuous succession of susceptible young panicles to attack across a season. Bacterial leaf blight (disease causing leaf-edge scorch/burning, caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) and sheath rot (caused by the fungus Sarocladium oryzae) are both noted as occurring, with bacterial leaf blight sometimes reaching damaging severity in some fields and causing yield loss. A separate leaf-browning condition attributed to Helminthosporium (brown spot) is noted as occurring generally in fields short of nitrogen, and is said to resolve on its own once adequate nitrogen fertilization is provided.
caveat: Brief secondary coverage only (this source's main pest/disease focus is brown planthopper); stem borer, bacterial leaf blight and brown spot are all already well documented elsewhere in this project from the separate CARDI 2007 book batches, so this entry is flagged as a likely near-total duplicate — kept mainly for the specific synchronized-flowering-time control tip for stem borer, which may not already be captured, and for the brown-spot-resolves-with-nitrogen observation.
